rationale: Start with a broad gradient to locate the six-compound elution window and identify critical pairs while minimizing the risk of missing late compounds. A moderate temperature leaves room to probe temperature-dependent selectivity in either direction.

The first method already achieves the maximum CRF of 1.000. Shortening only the gradient tests whether we can retain full resolution while reducing analysis time, with the critical pair currently comfortably resolved at R = 2.68.

Both methods already attain the maximum CRF; this run tests whether higher temperature can shorten retention while preserving full resolution. Holding the gradient fixed isolates temperature selectivity for the critical pair, now at R = 1.63.

At 50 C all pairs remain fully resolved, so shorten the gradient by one grid step to seek a faster method with the same maximum CRF. This tests the steepness limit while keeping temperature-dependent selectivity fixed.

Reduce the gradient slope by lowering phi1 while retaining the shorter gradient duration, aiming to restore the critical pair to R ≥ 1.5. The last peak previously eluted near 0.53 organic fraction, so phi1 = 0.80 leaves ample elution margin.

Shift the gradient window upward while preserving the slope of injection 5 to reduce retention without steepening the gradient. This tests whether a higher starting organic fraction preserves resolution, particularly for the early pair and the critical middle pair.

Slightly flatten the gradient to recover the middle pair's small resolution deficit while retaining the time savings from the higher starting organic fraction. This should offer a faster fully resolved method than injection 5.

Raise the starting organic fraction another step to shorten retention, while keeping phi1 fixed to make the gradient slightly shallower. The shallower slope may compensate for the middle-pair resolution loss seen when shifting the entire window upward.

Test a higher starting organic fraction to shorten the run, paired with a shallower gradient to protect the marginal middle-pair resolution. This also probes how much initial organic the early pair can tolerate before losing full resolution.

Increase the final organic fraction by one step to shorten the last-peak retention while holding the starting conditions and temperature fixed. This tests whether the middle pair's R = 1.72 margin can accommodate a slightly steeper gradient.

Maximum CRF is already secured, so test a much steeper gradient for a faster alternative after a possible middle-pair elution-order reversal. Using 40 C should give the early pair more separation than at 50 C, though the compressed middle and late pairs remain uncertain.

Keep the fast gradient fixed and lower temperature to test whether selectivity can resolve its sole deficient pair. This isolates temperature response in the steep-gradient regime while retaining the previously demonstrated maximum-score methods as fallbacks.

Return to the fully resolved 50 C region with a slope between injections 9 and 10, targeting R just above 1.5 and a last peak near 3.4 minutes. Trimming the endpoint to 0.60 should keep all peaks within the gradient while reducing its programmed duration.

Raise temperature one step while keeping injection 13's gradient fixed to test further time savings and middle-pair selectivity. The early pair may lose resolution, so this run probes the temperature limit rather than assuming the maximum CRF will be preserved.

Test whether a higher starting organic fraction can save time at a lower temperature that better separates the early pair. A shallower gradient aims to protect the middle pair, while the 0.55 endpoint provides margin above the recent last-peak elution composition.

Return to the maximum-score region and seek more resolution margin by lowering the starting organic fraction and slightly flattening the slope relative to injection 8. The trimmed endpoint should still elute all six compounds during the four-minute gradient.

Test whether injection 16's lower starting organic fraction provides enough early-pair separation to tolerate 55 C. Keeping its gradient fixed isolates the temperature effect and may shorten retention while preserving the maximum CRF.

Test the lower-temperature neighbor of injection 13, the fastest fully resolved method so far. Lower temperature should improve the early pair; this run checks whether the middle pair also remains above R = 1.5, establishing a more robust maximum-score operating region.

Maximum CRF is already secured; this run seeks a larger resolution margin in the fast operating region. A slightly shallower slope than injection 16 should improve the critical middle pair while keeping the early pair retained and the last peak well below 10 minutes.

Lower the endpoint one step from injection 13 to strengthen its marginal middle-pair resolution while preserving the early-pair separation. This tests a nearby maximum-score method with more resolution margin and only a modest expected increase in retention time.

Test the lower-temperature neighbor of injection 20: its shallower slope should compensate for the small middle-pair deficit observed at 45 C in injection 18. This seeks a nearby maximum-score method with stronger early-pair separation and ample margin below the 10-minute time threshold.

Test the lower-temperature neighbor of injection 16, whose middle-pair resolution has enough margin to potentially tolerate cooling. This should strengthen early-pair separation while retaining full resolution and a last-peak time comfortably below 10 minutes.

The maximum CRF is already secured, with injection 13 the fastest fully resolved method observed. Test a shallower neighboring gradient for greater resolution margin, keeping the first peak retained and the endpoint above the estimated last-peak elution composition.

Test the cooler neighbor of injection 23 to improve early-pair separation while using its middle-pair resolution margin to tolerate the temperature change. This should preserve the maximum CRF and establish a less temperature-sensitive alternative to the faster but marginally resolved injection 13.

Use a slope between the fully resolved injections 9 and 20 to target maximum CRF with more middle-pair resolution margin than the fastest method, injection 13. All peaks should elute well before the gradient ends, with the last peak expected near 3.6 minutes.
